images.title: Two leftover pairs make one more row of four
images.purpose: Shows 22 as 5 rows of 4 with 2 left and 6 as 1 row of 4 with 2 left; the two leftover pairs join into one full row, so 22 + 6 = 28 = 4 × 7.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two dot arrays side by side, with their leftover pairs meeting below in one new row.
images.exact_structure: Left array: 5 rows of 4 teal (#0072B2) dots (20 dots), and under it 2 dashed empty circles, labelled 22 above the array. Right array: 1 row of 4 teal (#0072B2) dots, and under it 2 dashed empty circles, labelled 6 above the array. Two thin grey (#6B7280) arrows lead from the two dashed pairs down to one new row of 4 amber (#E69F00) dots centred below both arrays, inside a reddish purple (#CC79A7) outlined rounded box, labelled 2 + 2 = 4. Under the new row, the line 28 = 4 × 7. In the two arrays the 2 + 2 leftover places are drawn only as dashed empty circles, so the filled dots are 24 teal plus 4 amber in the new row, 28 in all. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Two numbers that each leave 2 over a multiple of 4 add up to a multiple of 4.
images.description: Shows 22 as 5 rows of 4 with 2 left and 6 as 1 row of 4 with 2 left; the two leftover pairs join into one full row, so 22 + 6 = 28 = 4 × 7.
images.teaching_notes: The four amber dots in the new row are the same four leftovers moved down.

image_decisions.why: Dot rows of four make the leftover pairs joining into a full row visible.
